title: Higher-Order Orthogonal Inference with an Unknown Mildly Ill-Posed Operator
banked_reason: D0.5 certified the repaired note as mathematically sound at incremental tier, below the requested field floor; no bounded in-scope repair can lift the restrictive known-coordinate diagonal NPIV package to field level.
tldr: The general five-part validity package is preserved, including the bounded-center topology repair, the pointwise counterexample, the two directions of the neighborhood bridge, the compatibility hierarchy, and the spectral representation boundary. The econometric upgrade now fully exploits the maintained known aligned singular coordinates: only the unknown diagonal singular values are estimated, with separate coordinatewise thresholded structural, dual, and inverse blocks. This changes the inverse-defect rate to \(k_n^\zeta\sqrt{\log k_n/n}\). The feasible studentized theorem holds on \(1/(2\tau)<\kappa<\min\{m/[2(m\zeta+1)],1/(2\zeta+1)\}\); first order retains endpoint \(1/\{2(\zeta+1)\}\), while every fixed order \(m\geq2\) reaches the proved variance-limited endpoint \(1/(2\zeta+1)\). The remaining ceiling is not claimed minimax sharp.
gap: The parent identified pointwise-versus-neighborhood locality but delivered no estimator or inferential gain. Classical work already supplies higher-order scores, projections, and implicit-function recursion; first-order NPIV work supplies regular linear-functional inference; current stabilized HOIF work treats well-conditioned Gram matrices. The unresolved combined problem is whether genuine finite-variance higher-order compatibility can yield feasible studentized inference when a growing inverse operator is unknown and ill-posed.
fill: Relative to parent stat_hoif_neyman_orthogonality_frontier/v1 and along the fixed estimation axis, prove the counterexample, corrected two-way neighborhood bridge on the explicit density chart, compatibility hierarchy, and spectral representation boundary; then prove the exact foldwise NPIV chain bias, uniform training rates, termwise Hoeffding bounds for the actual symmetrized statistic, uniform variance consistency and studentized normal approximation, and strict gain over the same first-order learners. The field-level delta is the inference capability, while the general theory explains why its sieve correction is approximate rather than an exact infinite-dimensional kernel. The implementation is fully specified by a four-block cyclic split, three empirical cross-moment matrices, two loading vectors, population-scale singular-value thresholding, and an everywhere-positive variance estimate. The target repair fixes \(w\) across the class and lets \(\nu_{P0}(dx)=w(x)P0^X(dx)\) vary with the unknown marginal, eliminating the infeasible fixed-policy-density interpretation without adding estimation of \(w\).
